Temporary Course
Tags: courses
Short Description: A course approved for limited offerings, typically to test an experimental course or address a temporary need. Also known as an “X-Course.”
Temporary Course
UM 8.80.12 A temporary course may be offered no more than twice and only during a two-year period following its approval. A temporary course must meet one or more of the following criteria: a) it is experimental in nature. It is innovative, using unconventional devices or pedagogical methods, course materials, approach to course content or student-teacher relationships; b) it is being tried out on a temporary basis so that its value and effectiveness can be tested before it is added to a department’s permanent curriculum; c) it is intended for a limited duration, such as in the case of employing a visiting specialist temporarily available or to satisfy temporary needs and interests of students or to deal with timely issues.

UM 8.81.30 A Temporary Course shall have approval of the department(s) or committee proposing it, the dean(s) of the college(s) involved, and the Curriculum and Standards Committee and/or the Graduate Council, except that a temporary University College mini-course (a one-credit lower-level undergraduate course taught during the fall or spring semester) does not require the approval of the Curriculum and Standards Committee. The Curriculum and Standards Committee shall, however, receive information about any temporary University College mini-course after it has been approved by the college dean. The Graduate Council may refuse to grant or may attach conditions to the granting of graduate program credit for a temporary course. Each college may require internal channels of approval in addition to those specified here.

UM 8.81.31 The Curriculum and Standards Committee and the Graduate Council shall give priority at their meetings to the consideration of proposed temporary courses. Prior to approving temporary courses, these committees shall distribute to all faculty a description of these courses and shall provide faculty members with a seven-day period in which to register comments with the Chairperson of the Curriculum and Standards Committee and/or with the Dean of the Graduate School.
UM 8.81.60 It is the responsibility of the Office of Enrollment Services to limit the offering of a temporary course to only twice during a two-year period and to limit to three times the offering of a specific topic within an open-ended course.

Syllabus
Tags: courses
Short Description: A roadmap for a course that communicates its scope, learning outcomes, expectations, policies, assessments, and other essential information students need to successfully complete the course.
Syllabus
University Manual 8.50.30 Course Syllabi. All instructors shall make available a syllabus in the first week of class, or first day of class for fully-online accelerated programs (8.51.24), to students enrolled in each of their courses. Syllabi components should clearly communicate classroom policies, essential aspects of the course, and expectations of student participation.
University Manual 8.51.24 For online courses taught in the fully-online accelerated calendar, final projects and/or final exams shall be scheduled by faculty according to the learning outcomes of the class and best pedagogical practices for online learning. The calendar of due dates for assignments and assessments shall be in the syllabus and available to students on the first day of class. No final exam or final project shall be due after the last day of the session.
From the Provost:

In addition to satisfying Faculty Senate approved policies, your syllabus communicates mutual expectations between you and your students and serves as a roadmap to successful course completion, including your course scope, expectations, learning outcomes, deadlines, attendance policies, grading criteria, and other important information. Please provide students with information about assessment/major paper/project due dates, office hours, availability of special tutorial sessions, and expectations on individual vs group work. This clear outlining of expectations helps to ensure that students in your classes understand what they are expected to learn, how they will be assessed, and are fully aware of your academic standards. Providing such information can help avoid misunderstanding, frustration—on both sides—and foster acceptance of responsibility by our students

Complete the following fields with your contact information.

Academic Career Select the appropriate Academic Career from the available options. You may only choose one option. If you plan to offer this course in both the traditional and accelerated calendars, please provide a rationale in the Supporting Materials file upload gadget that comes after the description.
College Select the college in which the course is housed.
Department Select the department in which the course is housed.
Honors Program Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Honors Program.

General Education Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “No” is chosen for General Education.
Temporary Course Select Yes or No.

Subject Code The subject code must be owned by the College and Department previously entered in the form.
Number A validation error will occur if you use a number already in use by the subject code. The course numbering system is found in UM 8.30.10.
Temporary course numbers end with an “X”
Grand Challenge course numbers end with a “G”
Is this a 400-level course available for graduate credit? Required for all courses. Select Yes or No, regardless of the course level.
Course Title
Abbreviated Course Title 29-characters max.
Course Description Course descriptions are written for students, not faculty, and must communicate clearly and concisely to them. Jargon, acronyms, and technical language should be avoided as much as possible. Anyone should be able to read the description and understand the nature and intent of the course.
URI course descriptions include additional course information such as credits, cross-listed courses, method of instruction, class hours, requisites, grading, graduate credit, and general education outcomes. Descriptions will be formatted to the catalog standard prior to final approval.
Supporting Materials Optional. Use this file upload to provide additional information that may be helpful to review committees before the proposal enters the approval workflow.

Modality Select all applicable options to indicate whether the course will be offered in person, online, or both. The specific modalities are provided for reference next to the checkboxes and are also defined in University Manual 8.30.30
Method of Instruction All courses must have at least one method of instruction. Note that “Online” is not a method of instruction; it was removed from the list of methods of instruction in 2025.
If the course has multiple methods of instruction, select the first as Primary and all additional methods as Secondary.
If the course has two or more methods of instruction, indicate how the methods are divided. This information is important for Enrollment Services; omitting it may delay final approval.
Requisites Can include prerequisites, corequisites, antirequisites, or other enrollment requirements.

Is this a cross-listed course? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Is this a cross-listed course?
Cross-listed course(s) for eCampus Click “Add New” to add all cross-listings.
Cross-listed course(s) for the Catalog Click the “+” and add all cross-listings again.
Cross-listed Department(s) Add all departments belonging to the cross-listed courses, even if one or more belong to the same department.
Letter(s) of support from cross-listed departments For new courses and course modifications, the “parent” department (the department associated with the course code on the proposal) must provide a letter of support from each cross-listed department.
What if my cross-listed course code belongs to the same department as the parent course code? For example, MCE and ISE are both in the Department of Mechanical, Industrial & Systems Engineering.
Just upload a document stating: “Both subject codes belong to the same department.”

Can this course be repeated for credit? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Can this course be repeated for credit?
Maximum times course may be taken: Enter max number of times.
Maximum credits allowed: Enter the maximum number of credits a student may earn for the course. For example, a 3-credit course that may be taken three times for credit has a maximum of 9 credits.
Can students repeat within the same term? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Can students repeat within the same term?
Maximum credits allowed per term: Enter the maximum number of credits a student may earn from this course within a single term.

Explain the purpose of the course. Enter a brief explanation of the course's purpose.
How is this course used within the curriculum? Select the appropriate option from the provided radio buttons.
🔽 The following field will appear only if if Core requirement… is chosen from How is this course used within the curriculum?
List all degree, major, minor, and certificate programs for which this course is required. List the name of all applicable programs for which the course is a required component.
By checking this box, I acknowledge that all courses must be approved via Faculty Senate vote before a program can be reviewed for final approval. Check the box to acknowledge that the course must receive Faculty Senate approval before a program requiring the course can receive final approval.

This section is completed by the Department Chair or, when applicable, the Director, Area Coordinator, or College Curriculum Committee Chair. Proposers should leave this section blank and proceed to the next section.

Double Major
The completion of the requirements for two academic majors, with both majors leading to the same degree. For example, a student may complete two majors that each lead to a B.A. The student earns one degree, with both majors recorded on the permanent record and transcript.

Major Title
The formal name of the major associated with a student’s program of study, as approved by the University and listed in the University Catalog. The major title identifies the primary academic field or area of study in which the student completes the requirements of the program.

Kuali Curriculum Management (CM) is URI’s system for managing university curriculum and the curriculum approval process. It uses electronic forms and workflow to route course, program, and specialization proposals through the appropriate levels of review and approval.

Kuali serves as the central source for approved curriculum information:
Kuali CM — Manages curriculum proposals and the approval workflow.
Academic Catalog — Pulls approved course, program, and specialization information from Kuali.
eCampus — Receives approved course information from Kuali for implementation in future terms.

Information entered into Kuali can flow directly into the official academic catalog and eCampus. Proposals should therefore be clear, accurate, and unambiguous, as the information entered during the proposal process becomes part of the University’s official curriculum.
